title: Exercise every declared timing semantic in a bound telemetry test

facts.note: Tracking-plan files and test files carrying a Telemetry: header are identifiable by file kind/path.

values: repository has adopted the telemetry rule family and its tracking plan contains any item with a non-empty timing list (standing state, whether the item, its bound tests, or neither changed)
facts.note: Standing scope: every adopted item with declared timing is evaluated on every check, including plan-only changes and existing unchanged items. Needs a plan parser reading each item's timing list, an adoption check, and a binder resolving Telemetry: headers to items (validator bun_telemetry_test).

values: declared timing semantic not referenced by any bound test
facts.note: Lexical detector finding from bun_telemetry_test. It establishes only that a bound test references the behaviour; it does not prove runtime ordering.

fires: A tracking-plan item declares "timing": ["post-commit"] and no test bound to it via a Telemetry: header mentions commit in code or test title.
A plan-only change adds absent-after-rollback to an item whose existing, unchanged bound tests only assert return values, never rollback.
An existing, unchanged item declares correlation-across-async and the only mention of correlation/context is in a code comment or in the tracking-plan prose.
An item declares ["post-commit", "absent-after-rollback"] and bound tests reference commit but nothing references rollback.
doesNotFire: A diagnostic log or internal span whose tracking-plan item has an empty or absent timing list.
An item declaring only post-commit (its sole semantic) with a bound test whose title or assertions reference commit.
A repository that has not adopted the telemetry rule family (rule is inert until adoption).

given: In an adopted repository, a tracking-plan item declares timing semantics (post-commit, absent-after-rollback, correlation-across-async) in its timing list
when: The item and its Telemetry:-bound tests are evaluated — on any plan or test change, or for existing unchanged items
then: For each declared semantic, at least one bound test must reference the behaviour (commit, rollback, correlation/context) in code or a test title.
prefer: Declare on the item, name it in the bound test: "timing": ["post-commit"] with test("emits the planned event once the invocation commits", () => { ... }).
Assert the behaviour: emission only after commit, none after rollback, context kept across the async handoff.
avoid: Satisfying a semantic only via a test comment or tracking-plan prose.
Relying on return-value tests for transaction-time telemetry.
Claiming the lexical check proves ordering statically — false precision.
unless: The item declares no timing (empty timing list, e.g. diagnostic logs, internal spans).
The rule family is not yet adopted: the rule is inert until adoption.
why: Transaction-time bugs (event fired before its commit, rollback that still emits, context lost across an await) escape return-value tests; the plan declares when ordering matters, so bound tests must speak to it.
evidence: For every adopted tracking-plan item with a non-empty timing list (changed or not), each declared semantic is matched by at least one test bound via a Telemetry: header whose code or test title references commit / rollback / correlation-context respectively.
The bun_telemetry_test validator reports no timing-semantics finding.
verifier_detail: Semantic → behaviour mapping: post-commit = emission only after the transaction commits (look for 'commit'); absent-after-rollback = never emitted when the transaction rolls back (look for 'rollback'); correlation-across-async = correlation context continues across an async handoff (look for 'correlation'/'context').

Check is plan-driven and lexical by design: it requires the plan to say when ordering matters and the test to speak to it. Source of truth is the item's timing list; match only in test code or test titles, excluding comments and tracking-plan prose. It deliberately does not prove ordering statically — it cannot, and pretending otherwise would be false precision.

Scope: standing — every item with declared timing in an adopted repository, each semantic checked independently; only tests bound by a Telemetry: header count. Items with empty/absent timing are not judged (keeps diagnostic logs and internal spans out of scope). Inert until adoption, like every rule in this family.
audit: Source term ids: timing_semantic, exercised. Original name: 'Declared timing semantics are exercised by a bound test'.

sharedNodes.text: strict: the checker fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.text: Assert the behaviour: emission only after commit, none after rollback, context kept across the async handoff.
additions.justification: Derived directly from the timing_semantic term definitions (S008) to make the preferred move concrete; adds no obligation beyond referencing the behaviour.
